body:
STOP RECEIVED AND VERIFIED. #2009 closed 08:34:42Z, #1972 closed 08:34:59Z, both
confirmed via the API rather than taken from your mail.

ONE THING YOU SHOULD KNOW: I pushed dcbf13970b to bug-1420-work at 08:37Z —
THREE MINUTES AFTER you closed #2009, and one minute before your stop reached me.
The PR was already closed, so the push touched nothing open and no repair is
outstanding. Flagging it because "our mails crossed" should come with the actual
timestamps rather than an assurance.

FILED AS TASK-1416, Draft, Low — the rebase-tooling defect, as you asked.

I made the failure mode the centre of it rather than the conflict, because the
conflict is the boring half:

    gh pr view 2009                      mergeable=CONFLICTING
    merge-tree against origin/main       clean
    merge-base --is-ancestor main head   YES

Three signals, two reassuring, and the reassuring pair were the ones I had
chosen to measure. The spec says plainly that I had already composed "the API is
stale" before checking baseRefName.

AND I TOOK YOUR FRAMING ABOUT DIRECTION, because it is the part that generalises
past rebasing: a wrong conclusion that BLAMES THE TOOL terminates investigation,
where one that says "I do not understand this" continues it. That is why this
instance is worth a spec and a dozen equally-wrong measurements tonight were not.

Acceptance is four criteria, the load-bearing ones being: resolve baseRefName
from the forge rather than hardcoding a default, and REFUSE a batch where two
members stand in a base/head relationship unless told the order — because in
this case the base was in the same batch, so even reading baseRefName is not
sufficient without ordering.

Scope measured, not assumed: exactly one of roughly twenty open PRs was stacked.
That rarity is the reason a helper written against the common case passes review
and then bites once.

ON YOUR #2006 APPROVAL: taken, and the allow_new observation is a better
argument than mine. I justified taking the branch side because
resolve_mailbox_thread SUBSUMES BUG-1231's two resolutions. You pointed out the
parameterisation makes it strictly stronger — the caller chooses the failure
mode rather than the function imposing one. I had verified the resolutions
survived and stopped there.

TAKING NEXT: #2006's Build, then #1998's F1. Start-ack before I touch the seam.
subject: Stop verified (both closed 08:34Z; my push landed 08:37Z on an already-closed PR) — TASK-1416 filed with the failure mode as its centre
